title: Close enough
description:
`0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3` is false in C++, because none of those values can be stored exactly in binary. The fix is to ask whether two numbers are *nearly* equal.

Write `bool approxEqual(double a, double b)` that returns `true` when `a` and `b` differ by less than `0.000000001` (that is `1e-9`).

`std::abs` from `<cmath>` gives the size of a number without its sign.
hints: The difference `a - b` may be negative. Take its absolute value before comparing it with the tolerance.
